evidence: task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template environment/Dockerfile (both sha256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1), so it is template-controlled and unchanged. Against the skill's section-15 checklist: pinned base 'FROM node:22-bookworm-slim' (line 1, versioned tag, no --platform); 'ENV NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules' (line 3); 'npm install -g --no-audit --no-fund express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1' (lines 9-11, exact versions); 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/' and 'COPY assets/ /assets/' (lines 14-15), both sources exist (environment/instructions/{hireops_rules.md,integration.md}, environment/assets/seed_data.json) and cover every /instructions and /assets path the brief names (instruction.md:11 /instructions/hireops_rules.md, /instructions/integration.md; instruction.md:15 /assets/seed_data.json); 'chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets' (line 16); /app created, git-initialised and committed with only .gitkeep (lines 17-23). No COPY/ADD of solution/ or tests/. Runtime dependency closure: the golden requires only express, better-sqlite3 and Node built-ins (crypto, fs, path, node:http, node:worker_threads); solution/app/package.json pins exactly express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1, matching the image. No run-time install anywhere: solve.sh does no npm/apt install (it copies app files and resets the DB), test.sh contains no npm/install step, and the brief tells the builder 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages' (instruction.md:15) and integration.md:3-4,18-19 says Express and better-sqlite3 are available through NODE_PATH. test.sh launches with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules, consistent with the agent image ENV. task.toml sets no [environment].docker_image, so the Dockerfile is not shadowed. tests/Dockerfile installs the same express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1 on a node:22-bookworm-slim-derived /usr/local, so agent and grading runtimes agree. Notes (not defects): apt packages (ca-certificates git procps sqlite3) are unpinned, which check-dockerfiles.py treats as NOTE; the base is a version tag, not a digest, as in the template. Colderwater lessons checked: none of lessons 1-21 concerns the agent Dockerfile directly; lesson 19/20 Docker-harness patterns are verifier-side. Counterexample probes: a broken app needing an extra package (e.g. ws) cannot install it and fails at grade time, which is fair because the brief forbids installs and names the allowed packages; a conforming alternative using only Express, better-sqlite3 and Node built-ins (resolved via NODE_PATH, no local node_modules) runs in this image and in the verifier image, so no conforming app is penalised by the image. Measurement gap stated honestly: this round's raw evidence (via-solve.log, workspace.json) ran in the verifier image hireops-verifier:20261002-permission-repair, not in a freshly built agent image; the agent image itself was not built in this review (no Docker started per assignment). The identical global npm install line built successfully in that verifier image on Debian bookworm and better-sqlite3 loaded there, which supports buildability, but a direct agent-image build log is not part of this round's evidence. The row's documented verification is structural and is fully satisfied by source, so this gap is recorded but not treated as a required missing measurement.
